design.effect_definition: Cohen's d = (max mu_j - min mu_j)/sigma for the k=3 families (equally spaced means at (-d/2, 0, +d/2)); d = delta/sigma for the one-sample family; the scale family uses the sd ratio sigma_max/sigma_min
design.size_adjustment: the size-adjusted test is the SAME procedure with its critical value recalibrated to attain alpha exactly: the threshold is the empirical (1-alpha) quantile of the calibration statistic under H0 with the same parent, n and N, where the calibration statistic is the statistic itself for upper-tail rules (F, chi-square), |statistic| for the two-sided t test and |S - n/2| for the two-sided sign test. This keeps the nominal and calibrated rejection regions nested, so a liberal test necessarily loses power when size-adjusted and a conservative test necessarily gains it. A distribution-free 95% order-statistic CI for the threshold is reported together with the power range it induces
design.common_random_numbers: all tests of a family are evaluated on identical simulated data sets; pairwise differences therefore use a paired McNemar-layout interval, cross-checked against Newcombe unpaired, and the wider of the two is used for the verdict
design.comparison_rule: a power ordering is claimed only when the conservative 95% difference CI excludes 0; otherwise the verdict is "inconclusive"
design.size_distortion_direction: size_distortion is "liberal" when the 95% CI of alpha-hat lies entirely above 0.05 (nominal-alpha power overstates discrimination), "conservative" when entirely below (nominal-alpha power understates discrimination), else "none"; nominal_power_contaminated is true whenever the CI excludes 0.05 in either direction

equivalence.note: Same-data differences are floating-point level; the archive alpha-hat comparison is a two-sample Monte Carlo comparison and is judged by a 3-sigma z-criterion, because a fixed tolerance of 0.005 is inside the Monte Carlo noise at N=2000 for large rates (Bartlett under skewness).

The nominal-alpha power of a test whose size CI excludes 0.05 is flagged nominal_power_contaminated = true; such numbers must not be used to rank tests.

For the discrete statistics (sign test, median test) the calibrated critical value attains a size strictly below 0.05 (see adjusted_size_attainment), so their size-adjusted power is mildly conservative and part of any gap to a continuous competitor reflects discreteness, not discrimination.

power_adjusted_ci_combined is the union of the Wilson interval for the power estimate and the power range induced by the 95% CI of the calibrated critical value; it is a conservative envelope, not a nominal 95% interval.
